--- title: "Step 3: Population shifts towards or away from congeners" subtitle: Vocal character displacement in southern capuchinos author: Marcelo Araya-Salas date: "2026-10-07" toc: true toc-depth: 4 toc-location: left number-sections: true highlight-style: pygments format: html: df-print: kable code-fold: true code-tools: true css: qmd.css editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # options to customize chunk outputs knitr::opts_chunk$set( message = FALSE ) ``` ::: ::: {.alert .alert-info} # Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted} - Evaluate whether populations that co-occur with a congener are acoustically closer to (convergence) or farther from (divergence) that congener's song than conspecific populations that do not co-occur with it ::: The sympatry models (Step 2) show whether heterospecific songs are more or less different in sympatry, but a dyadic comparison cannot tell which species changed. Here we ask, for each focal species, whether populations that co-occur with a given congener are acoustically closer to (convergence) or farther from (divergence) that congener's song than conspecific populations that do not co-occur with it. - Pairs are always oriented as focal song × congener song. - Pairs recorded at the same locality (the sympatric comparisons used in Step 2) are excluded. Congener songs therefore act as an external reference, and this test does not reuse the Step 2 contrast. - `cooccur = 1` when the focal population's locality also has the congener. - A shift can only be tested when the focal species has at least one population with the congener and at least one without it, and when the congener was also recorded at a locality other than the co-occurring focal population(s). Combinations that fail either condition are listed but not modelled. For example, iberaensis and palustris were recorded only at E_Ibera. Once same-locality pairs are removed, the E_Ibera hypoxantha population has no congener songs to be compared with, so hypoxantha vs. iberaensis and hypoxantha vs. palustris cannot be tested this way. # Load packages and custom functions {.unnumbered .unlisted} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install knitr package if not installed if (!requireNamespace("sketchy", quietly = TRUE)) { install.packages("sketchy") } packages <- c( "knitr", "dplyr", "tidyverse", "vegan", "ecodist", "brms", github = "maRce10/brmsish", "kableExtra", "ggplot2", "ggtext", "ggh4x", github = "stan-dev/cmdstanr" ) # install/load packages sketchy::load_packages(packages = packages) options(knitr.kable.NA = '', brms.file_refit = "never") # set theme globally theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 20)) # custom functions (shared by all reports) source("./scripts/functions.R") ``` ::: # Load data {.unnumbered .unlisted} Pairwise data sets created in [Data preparation](0_data_preparation.qmd). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} step_inputs_simple <- readRDS("./data/processed/step_inputs_simple.rds") pairs_simple <- step_inputs_simple$pairs occ_simple <- step_inputs_simple$occ step_inputs_complex <- readRDS("./data/processed/step_inputs_complex.rds") pairs_complex <- step_inputs_complex$pairs occ_complex <- step_inputs_complex$occ ``` ::: # Simple songs ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shift_combos_simple <- shift_combinations(occ_simple) print(shift_combos_simple) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: $$ \begin{split} \text{acoustic distance}_{\text{focal, congener}} &\sim \text{cooccur} \\ &\quad + (1 \mid \text{focal population}) + (1 \mid \text{congener population}) \\ &\quad + (1 \mid \text{focal individual}) + (1 \mid \text{congener individual}) \end{split} $$ Because pairs are oriented, focal and congener populations (and individuals) enter as separate crossed random effects rather than as multi-membership terms. The co-occurrence effect is a property of focal populations. It is therefore evaluated against the variation among focal populations (`sd(pop1)`), which is the appropriate and conservative unit of replication given the very small number of populations involved. The response is standardized within each focal–congener dataset, with the same regularizing priors as in Step 1. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shift_models_simple <- list() shift_dat_simple <- list() for (k in which(shift_combos_simple$testable)) { focal <- shift_combos_simple$focal[k] congener <- shift_combos_simple$congener[k] nm <- paste(focal, "vs", congener, sep = "_") shift_dat_simple[[nm]] <- population_shift_data( pairs = pairs_simple, focal = focal, congener = congener, occ = occ_simple ) shift_models_simple[[nm]] <- brm( acoustic_distance_sc ~ cooccur + (1 | pop1) + (1 | pop2) + (1 | individual1) + (1 | individual2), data = shift_dat_simple[[nm]], family = gaussian(), prior = priors_ws, cores = 4, chains = 4, iter = 10000, backend = "cmdstanr", threads = threading(8), control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 15), file = paste0("./data/processed/fits/population_shift_", nm, "_simple_fit") ) } ``` ::: Prior predictive checks for the population shift models: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} for (nm in names(shift_dat_simple)) { prior_only_shift <- brm( acoustic_distance_sc ~ cooccur + (1 | pop1) + (1 | pop2) + (1 | individual1) + (1 | individual2), data = shift_dat_simple[[nm]], family = gaussian(), prior = priors_ws, sample_prior = "only", chains = 2, iter = 2000, cores = 2, seed = 123, backend = "cmdstanr", file = paste0("./data/processed/fits/prior_only_population_shift_", nm, "_simple") ) # base::print - the document redefines print() as a kable wrapper base::print(prior_check_plot( prior_only_shift, paste0("Prior predictive check (simple songs, ", gsub("_vs_", " vs. ", nm), ")") )) } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](3_population_shifts_files/figure-html/prior predictive check population shift simple-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](3_population_shifts_files/figure-html/prior predictive check population shift simple-2.png){width=672} ::: ::: Mean acoustic distance from each focal population to the congener's songs recorded elsewhere (points: population means; bars: 95% intervals of the mean): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shift_plot_dat_simple <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(shift_dat_simple), function(nm) { x <- shift_dat_simple[[nm]] agg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(x, x$focal_population), function(p) { data.frame( focal_population = p$focal_population[1], cooccur = p$cooccur[1], mean = mean(p$acoustic_distance), se = sd(p$acoustic_distance) / sqrt(nrow(p)) ) })) agg$comparison <- gsub("_vs_", " vs. ", nm) agg })) ggplot(shift_plot_dat_simple, aes(x = focal_population, y = mean, color = cooccur)) + geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se), size = 0.8) + facet_wrap(~ comparison, scales = "free_x") + scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", begin = 0.3, end = 0.7, labels = c("0" = "No", "1" = "Yes"), name = "Co-occurs\nwith congener") + labs(x = "Focal population", y = "Acoustic distance to congener") + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](3_population_shifts_files/figure-html/population shift plot simple-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Co-occurrence effects (negative = focal populations living with the congener are closer to its song, i.e. convergence; positive = divergence): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shift_tab_simple <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(shift_models_simple), function(nm) { fe <- as.data.frame(fixef(shift_models_simple[[nm]]))["cooccur1", ] data.frame( Comparison = gsub("_vs_", " vs. ", nm), Estimate = round(fe$Estimate, 3), SE = round(fe$Est.Error, 3), `l-95% UI` = round(fe$Q2.5, 3), `u-95% UI` = round(fe$Q97.5, 3), `UI excludes 0` = ifelse(fe$Q2.5 > 0 | fe$Q97.5 < 0, "yes", "no"), check.names = FALSE ) })) print(shift_tab_simple) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
